sources.name: JMultiWOZ Japanese Multi-Domain Wizard-of-Oz Dataset v1.0
sources.authors_or_organization: Atsumoto Ohashi, Ryu Hirai, Shinya Iizuka, and Ryuichiro Higashinaka; Nagoya University Dialogue System Research Group
sources.version: JMultiWOZ 1.0 archive at the upstream master commit pinned below; one 64/24 pilot and one 512/64 scaled follow-up with fresh development dialogues

license.copyright_notice: The authors license the JMultiWOZ dataset under CC BY-SA 4.0 and explicitly state in their repository that models trained using it are not considered copies or direct derivatives of the dataset and do not need to comply with that license.
license.attribution_requirement: Credit Ohashi et al. (2024), link the JMultiWOZ repository and CC BY-SA 4.0 license, describe transformations, and do not imply author endorsement.
license.terms_review: The upstream dataset README, Hugging Face card, paper, license, and exact v1.0 archive were reviewed. The upstream repository explicitly permits model training and says resulting models are not copies or direct derivatives subject to CC BY-SA. The dataset contains Japanese human-simulated Wizard-of-Oz travel conversations with dialogue-state labels; its database sources are described by the authors as government or municipal and copyright-unencumbered official sites. This admission is limited to two local exploratory runs using deterministic samples from official train and dev splits: 64/24 for the first pilot, then 512/64 for a scaled follow-up whose dev sample excludes all 24 earlier public-dev dialogues. Both runs redact phone-like spans and omit phone, address, and reference slots. Raw data and weights remain local. Preserve attribution and recheck exact terms and artifact lineage before public distribution; this is a scoped source review, not legal advice.

transformations: Use the last four utterances before the final annotated SYSTEM turn as model context.
Serialize the final active domain, non-null active-domain arguments plus general city, and final SYSTEM reply as compact UTF-8 JSON.
Replace phone-like number spans with [PHONE] and omit phone, address, and reference slots.
filters: The first local exploratory run uses 64 deterministically selected official-train dialogues and 24 disjoint official-dev dialogues.

The scaled local exploratory follow-up uses 512 deterministically selected official-train dialogues and 64 official-dev dialogues, selected after excluding all 24 public-dev dialogue IDs used by the first run.
The scaled follow-up is fixed to seed 314159, 20 epochs, learning rate 0.01, and at most 10,240 per-example Adam updates; no additional seed sweep or hyperparameter search is admitted by this scope.
Do not use the public test split, remaining train/dev items, backend database files, participant account identifiers, or goal-description templates in either pilot.
Keep the archive, normalized examples, per-item selection manifests, predictions, and model artifacts outside every Git worktree; commit no source text or trained weights.
Keep the 101-case Codex-generated draft and every derivative excluded from training, tokenizer fitting, evaluation, filtering, prompt construction, and release evidence.
deduplication: Select and audit by dialogue ID and dialogue family; require disjoint official train/dev families and check item-content hashes for exact cross-split duplicates before training.
Record the exact upstream archive and source-member SHA-256 values plus selected per-dialogue content hashes in the local selection manifest.

review.rationale: The archive was downloaded from the authors' repository at commit a78dd334b907e12318b76bb23d0a9ed1498b8d15 and its SHA-256 and key JSON-member hashes were verified. Upstream files identify 4,246 Japanese dialogues across six task-oriented domains and official 3,646/300/300 train/dev/test splits. Two bounded local scopes are admitted: the original deterministic 64/24 pilot and a fixed-seed 512/64 follow-up whose public development IDs exclude the original 24. The two scopes contain 600 unique dialogue records in total; the scaled run validates its own 576 selected records before training. Raw source text and model artifacts remain outside Git.

sources.name: MASSIVE 1.1 English and Japanese intent and slot pilot
sources.authors_or_organization: Amazon Science MASSIVE; English source text from SLURP; localized by the MASSIVE authors and annotators
sources.version: MASSIVE 1.1 official archive at commit f966f21846043aabef9b0f974fa7970027f43738; 256 aligned train and 64 aligned public-dev IDs, each in en-US and ja-JP

license.copyright_notice: The pinned MASSIVE README, archive LICENSE, and NOTICE declare CC BY 4.0; NOTICE identifies the English SLURP source text as CC BY 4.0.
license.attribution_requirement: Credit Amazon Science, the MASSIVE and SLURP authors as identified by the release, link the dataset and CC BY 4.0 license, describe changes, and do not imply endorsement.
license.terms_review: The pinned 1.1 archive, repository README, LICENSE, NOTICE, and source paper were reviewed. This admission covers only 256 deterministic official-train ID families and 64 disjoint public-dev ID families, with both en-US and ja-JP rows for each ID. The source declares CC BY 4.0 and supports local model training and public-dev diagnostics subject to attribution. All output weights remain local; this source record does not resolve whether particular trained weights reproduce protected expression or approve public weight distribution. Re-review the exact artifact and complete lineage before public release. This is a scoped source review, not legal advice.

transformations: Use utt as the model input and parse bracketed slot annotations from annot_utt; use intent as the structured intent label.
Prefix each utterance with its en-US or ja-JP locale and serialize the intent and extracted slot values as compact UTF-8 JSON.
Do not use worker_id, the public test split, or any rows outside the deterministic 256-train-family and 64-dev-family cohort; scan selected text and slot values for email and phone patterns.
filters: Use 256 deterministic aligned ID families from official train and 64 disjoint aligned ID families from official dev, each represented once in en-US and once in ja-JP.
Retain dev rows only as a public exploratory structured-output diagnostic; never use them for training or tokenizer fitting.
Keep raw archive, normalized examples, item records, predictions, and model weights outside Git; commit no dataset text or weights.
The 101-case Codex draft and all derivatives remain excluded from training, tokenizer fitting, evaluation, filtering, prompt construction, and release evidence.
deduplication: Treat aligned en-US and ja-JP rows with the same source ID as one semantic family, not independent families.
Keep official train and dev family IDs disjoint and record a source-row hash and transformed-sample hash for every selected locale row.

review.reviewed_by: Codex-assisted pinned-archive, license, and scoped-item review
review.rationale: The official 1.1 archive and English/Japanese member hashes are pinned. The two locale files have matching row IDs and train/dev/test splits, with 60 aligned intent labels. A deterministic 256/64 family selection was inspected: all selected annotation brackets parse, all paired labels agree, and no selected text or slot value matched the email or phone scan. The dataset is localized device-assistant language, not spontaneous Japanese or English/Japanese code-switching; no qualified Lumi language review is claimed.

sources.name: JECS Japanese-English code-switching speech corpus v1 neutral transcript text
sources.authors_or_organization: Shinnosuke Takamichi, Yoshifumi Nakano, Ai Morimatsu, Takaaki Saeki, and Hiroshi Saruwatari; underlying JEC Basic Sentence Data credited to the Kurohashi-Kawahara Laboratory at Kyoto University and the NICT MASTAR Project Multilingual Translation Laboratory
sources.version: JECS v1; only the Japanese, English, and code-switched transcript text members plus the upstream README

license.copyright_notice: The JECS author page identifies the transcript text as CC BY 3.0 and treats the speech audio separately. JECS describes its text as based on JEC Basic Sentence Data, which JAIST catalogs as CC BY 3.0.
license.attribution_requirement: Credit the JECS authors, identify the JEC Basic Sentence Data and its credited laboratories, link the source and CC BY 3.0 terms, describe transformations, and do not imply endorsement.
license.terms_review: The JECS author page, README, Creative Commons deed, upstream JEC resource page, and JAIST language-resource catalog were reviewed. This local admission covers only the three exact neutral transcript text members and README, totaling 2,977 rows. Audio files and the other archive members were not acquired or used; the author page states distinct restrictions for audio. Text reuse and adaptation require attribution and other CC BY 3.0 conditions. This source review permits the bounded text-only pretraining and public-development measurement recorded here, but does not decide whether resulting weights are derivative works or clear those weights for public distribution. Reassess the exact artifact, all data lineage, and applicable third-party rights before any release. This is a scoped research review, not legal advice.

transformations: Read only the exact transcripts_ja.txt, transcripts_en.txt, transcripts_cs.txt, and README.md files whose individual SHA-256 hashes are recorded below; do not acquire or process audio or other archive members.
Parse JECSNNNN_LANG transcript rows, remove utterance identifiers, and remove the paired asterisk delimiters from code-switch examples while retaining their text.
Assign all language rows sharing a JECS numeric family ID to one deterministic training or development partition; record source-line and normalized-sample hashes in controlled local provenance files.
Apply email, URL, and phone-like sequence scans. Use fixed UTF-8 byte codes and language tags; no tokenizer is learned.
filters: Use only the three neutral transcript text members and their matching README; the full 374,577,780-byte ZIP and its audio were not downloaded or opened.

Pin the exact acquired member hashes: transcripts_ja.txt 20551876ae990563b2fda3b107fb3c5249e485d5b01847452f26a2f7956d2b5e; transcripts_en.txt a4d2e8980d42e8747e2e670c9d112953bd8298da292ba43c1bd2ffa6f8ffc083; transcripts_cs.txt 7c26eea872f3099e205035973c0784fcaa473c89f26018a5b4a1a6d72a2e468c; README.md 4d68ea0502e58698e245f104098f4dd9679e07398a4d44bc95b586732536f10d.

Keep raw text, item-level records, predictions, and trained weights in controlled local storage outside Git. The short pilot is exploratory and is not a conversational-quality or public-release approval.
deduplication: Group aligned language rows by numeric JECS utterance family before assigning the deterministic split.
Reject duplicate text within a language and any identical normalized sample that crosses the training/development boundary; the pilot also audits exact cross-language duplicate hashes.

review.reviewed_by: Codex-assisted primary-source, rights, and structural audit
review.rationale: The author-hosted source page identifies a CC BY 3.0 text license; the upstream JEC resource and JAIST catalog provide separate attribution context. Only four individually hashed text/evidence members were acquired by validated ZIP byte ranges. The Japanese and English IDs align across 1,219 families, the 539 code-switch rows are drawn from those families, and the train/development partition keeps each family together. Exact duplicate-hash and privacy-pattern checks are recorded by the pilot. These are structural checks only: this acted/read parallel speech corpus is not spontaneous ZenStream conversation, and qualified semantic or native-speaker quality review is not claimed.

sources.name: CSR-L Japanese-English HumanEval public-test query slice
sources.authors_or_organization: CSR-L authors Qingcheng Zeng, Yuheng Lu, Zeqi Zhou, Heli Qi, Puxuan Yu, Fuheng Zhao, Hitomi Yanaka, Weihao Xuan, and Naoto Yokoya; UTokyo-Yokoya-Lab; underlying HumanEvalRetrieval authors
sources.version: 158 Japanese-English HumanEval retrieval queries in the public test split

license.copyright_notice: The README at the pinned Hugging Face revision declares MIT for this dataset. It identifies the underlying mteb/HumanEvalRetrieval source as MIT.
license.attribution_requirement: Retain the MIT copyright and permission notice and cite the CSR-L paper and dataset, plus the underlying HumanEval source as requested by the dataset card. Identify the exact Japanese-English public-test slice and describe transformations.
license.terms_review: The exact Hugging Face dataset revision, README, and Japanese-English test member were pinned. The README declares MIT and identifies the underlying HumanEvalRetrieval source as MIT. The ACL paper states that the paper authors rewrote queries, with a second bilingual annotator validating or editing/discarding each rewrite, and lists the Japanese-English HumanEval slice as 158 queries. This record approves only evaluation of the exact Japanese-English HumanEval public-test queries in a local next-byte transfer probe. It does not admit the corpus, qrels, Chinese queries, other CSR-L tasks, any training/tokenizer/filtering/generation use, a sealed holdout, or public model-artifact distribution. No raw query text, predictions, or weights are committed. Re-review all data and exact artifact lineage before any model release. This is a scoped source review, not legal advice.

transformations: Select only config queries_ja_en, split test, from the pinned HumanEvalRetrieval-CSR-L revision; preserve each query text exactly as published.
Encode query text as UTF-8 bytes with the existing code-switch language tag, BOS, and EOS for next-byte evaluation of already-trained JECS checkpoints.
Do not read or use corpus documents, relevance judgments, Chinese-English queries, other task configurations, answers, or retrieved results.
filters: Use all and only the 158 unique Japanese-English HumanEval public-test query rows in queries_ja_en/test-00000-of-00001.parquet at revision d7634f8e08cf9249cdb2169fb153b0de85d705c8.
Use the public test as an external diagnostic, not as a sealed holdout or a training/development source.
Keep the raw dataset, normalized query text, item records, predictions, and model weights outside Git; commit metadata and aggregate results only.
The 101-case Codex draft and all derivatives remain excluded from training, tokenizer fitting, evaluation, filtering, prompt construction, and release evidence.
deduplication: Require one unique source query ID and one unique UTF-8 text hash per row.
Compare exact UTF-8 text hashes against all 2,977 eligible JECS training/development samples; reject any overlap.

review.reviewed_by: Codex-assisted primary-source, pin, rights, and sample-scope review
review.rationale: The immutable revision, README license declaration, test member size and LFS SHA-256, ACL description of human rewriting and validation, 158-row Japanese-English HumanEval scope, unique IDs/text, privacy-pattern flags, and exact-hash overlap against eligible JECS records were checked. Two rows match a generic phone-like digit pattern, but manual inspection shows only code/date examples, not contact details. The slice is admitted solely for one local next-byte transfer measurement; the public-test status and retrieval-query domain limit any quality claim.
